sentences.text: Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. The application is disposed of.

3.  The present petition has been filed seeking quashing of FIR No.449/2021, under Sections 498A/406/377/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) registered at Police Station Jagat Puri on the ground of settlement.
4. The petitioner no.2 is the husband of the respondent no.2 and the petitioners no.1, 3 and 4 are family members of the petitioner no.2.
The marriage of the petitioner no.2 and the respondent no.2 was solemnized on 15th March, 2012, according to Muslim rites and ceremonies.
Two children

5. Disputes arose between the parties and their respective families, which resulted in filing of the FIR by the respondent no.2 against the petitioners.

sentences.text:
Subsequently, the parties have settled their disputes before the Delhi Mediation Centre,
Karkardooma Courts in terms of Settlement Agreement dated 1st February, 2022, entered into between the parties, annexed as Annexure P-1 to the petition.
The parties have also been granted divorce by mutual consent.
7. As per the settlement, a sum of Rs.7,50,000/- was payable to the respondent no.2.
Out of the aforesaid amount, a sum of Rs.5,50,000/- has already been paid.

The petitioners have brought a demand draft of Rs.2,00,000/- in Court today and the same has been handed over to the respondent no.2.
8.
Issue notice.

9. Notice is accepted by the learned APP appearing on behalf of the State and by the respondent no.
2 appearing in person.
10. The respondent no.2 is present in Court and has been identified by the Investigating Officer (IO).
She informs the Court that she has settled the matter of her own free will and without any coercion.

She further states that she has no objection to quashing of the FIR.
11.
The petitioners are also present in Court and have been identified by their counsel.
They affirm the statement of the respondent no.2 and undertake to abide by the terms of settlement arrived at between the parties.
12. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 11/11/2023 at 10:07:04 continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the aforementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
13. There are two minor children born from the wedlock, who are in the care and custody of the respondent no.2/mother.
It is directed that the settlement executed between the petitioners and respondent no.2 as well as this order shall have no effect on the rights of the minor children in the future.
14. Consequently, FIR No.449/2021 registered at Police Station Jagat Puri and proceedings pursuant thereto are quashed.
15. The petition stands disposed of.

AMIT BANSAL, J.
